newsitem.title: FRANCE: French CNP sees 1997 net profits up 4-5 pct.
newsitem.headline: French CNP sees 1997 net profits up 4-5 pct.

text.p: French insurance firm CNP's net profits should increase by four to five percent this year, chief executive Pierre Darnis said on Monday.

"We will have a very slight increase in turnover in 1997. If we reach 103 or 104 billion francs, we will be content. On the other hand, the net profit should go up by four to five percent compared to 1996. That seems to us to be more significant," Darnis told a news conference.
CNP reported a net attributable profit for 1996 of 1.57 billion francs on turnover of 100.5 billion francs.
Darnis denied a media report that he would step down in June, at the end of his current mandate.
"I read with a bit of surprise that I was expected to leave," he said. "I don't feel too old to seek another mandate."
State-owned CNP is scheduled to be listed on the Paris Bourse in September.
